_capture.method: fetched with the Arena fetch tool (no key, no auth), 3 response chunks. The development sandbox has no outbound network to this host; CI does.
_capture.completeness: FIELD-PRESERVING EXCERPT. The Dallas 2026-27 roster returned 3 arrays (`forwards`, `defensemen`, `goalies`); this file retains 2 forwards, 2 defensemen and ALL 4 goalies verbatim for the fields this project stores (id, firstName.default, lastName.default, sweaterNumber, positionCode, shootsCatches, height/weight, birthDate, birthCity/birthCountry/birthStateProvince). Headshots were dropped. No retained value was edited.
why_it_matters: The `players` table has existed since schema v1 and has been EMPTY in every committed ledger: `NhlApi.roster()` was implemented but never called by any ingest stage. Requirement 10 asks for normalized storage of players and rosters, and requirement 2 asks for player/roster research; an empty table satisfies neither. This capture is the evidence that the feed is keyless, free, JSON and per-season, so the ingest can be wired up.

It also gives the injury feed something to join to. `injuries` rows carry a NAME and a team abbrev only (`Ryan Poehling`, `ANA`), so an injury could never be tied to a player_id; the roster publishes both, per club, per season.

Goalie names in the roster are the vocabulary the NHL's own per-game goalie log uses, so a probable starter read from ESPN (a different id space: ESPN player 3069285 = Linus Ullmark) can be resolved to an NHL player_id BY NAME, and that resolution is recorded as DERIVED with its match basis rather than asserted.
caveats: Shape is not uniform: `sweaterNumber` is absent for some players (Teddy Blueger, Brendan Brisson, Brandon Buhr on the TOR roster) and `shootsCatches` is absent for at least one defenseman (Jack Anderson, retained below). The parser must tolerate both.

This is a PRESEASON roster (retrieved 2026-09-22): it lists camp invitees and prospects (e.g. Jaxon Fuder, born 2006-04-02, on the Dallas roster) alongside NHL regulars. It is not the opening-night roster and must not be read as one.
The endpoint has no documented licence or rate limit; it is the same unofficial api-web host this project already depends on for schedules and results.

defensemen._note: retained to document that `shootsCatches` is OPTIONAL in the real payload

goalies._note: the response was truncated inside this record at `"birthCity":{"default":`, so the birthplace fields are OMITTED here rather than filled in. Everything retained was read off the payload.
